title: Operator Secret Swivel and Blinded Evidence Retention — PRD (draft)
content:
Purpose

This PRD proposes a product for rotating operator-facing secrets ("secret swivel") in private deployments and for generating compact, privacy-preserving audit evidence

that can be handed to customers and internal compliance without exposing full secrets, configuration diffs, or
PII. The goal is to enable quick operator remediation and audits while minimizing retained sensitive surface area
and giving customer-managed networking teams confidence in handoffs.

Context and problem statement

Private deployments require operator access patterns that occasionally need direct intervention (certificate rotates,
edge connector rekeys, temporary escalation for troubleshooting). Current approaches either:
- store full verbose audit payloads for forensic needs (high retention cost, raises risk), or
- redact aggressively (loses signal for root cause), or
- force manual evidence extraction (slow, error-prone).

Customers also require approval gates for network-affecting changes (firewall, peering, route maps) with verifiable
evidence that the gate was exercised and attestation for the change without leaking network topology or secret material.

Design goals (high level)
- Operator secret swivel: enable automated, auditable, reversible secret rotation flows that are operator-triggered but
  customer-consented when required.
- Blinded evidence capsule: produce a cryptographically-auditable, compact artifact that proves who did what, when,
  and which resources were affected while hiding sensitive fields (secrets, internal IPs) via deterministic blinding.
- Minimal retention: store compact artifacts for a configurable period with tiered granularity (short-term full, long-term
  compact hashes).
- Approval gate integration: wire evidence capsules into existing approval gate flow so approvals and fallbacks are
  captured as part of the artifact.
- Operability & UX: low-friction operator tooling (CLI and Console) that shows redacted context and quick rollback actions.

Key concepts and terminology
- Secret Swivel: operator-initiated rotation/replace sequence for a secret (API key, TLS cert, PSK) with optional
  customer acknowledgment. Swivel implies an automated swap, test, and rollback window.
- Evidence Capsule: an immutable, signed payload containing an event summary, blinded diffs, cryptographic receipts,
  and pointers to ephemeral debug bundles (if allowed).
- Blinding: deterministic replacement of sensitive tokens/addresses with consistent pseudonyms (e.g., ip-XXXX) so
  artifacts remain useful for debugging while disclosing no secrets.
- Compact Proofset: short hashes and Merkle roots summarizing larger logs for long-term retention and external audit.

Functional requirements
1) Secret swivel flow (operator side)
   - Start swivel: operator selects secret, provides reason, chooses rotation mode (immediate, staged, canary).
   - Customer consent: if secret affects customer-managed networking (e.g., peering keys), allow automated consent request
     delivered to the customer's admin channel (email, webhook). Swivel proceeds after policy configuration or explicit OK.
   - Swap & smoke test: platform performs rotation, runs smoke tests (connectivity, TLS handshake), reports pass/fail.
   - Rollback window: if smoke fails or operator cancels, automatic rollback within configurable timeframe.
   - Finalize: on success, platform stores evidence capsule and short-term debug bundle (if customer agreed).

2) Evidence capsule format (human-readable + machine-verifiable)
   - Header: capsule id, timestamp, actors (operator id, customer admin id if consented), action type, target resource id(s).
   - Blinded diff: JSON-style diff with sensitive fields replaced by deterministic placeholders.
   - Receipts: signatures (platform operator key, optional customer key), and Merkle root(s) for underlying logs.
   - Policy snapshot: which approval gate policy evaluated (name, version) and decision path.
   - Pointers: URL or object id for ephemeral debug bundle (0–1, only if allowed and TTL-limited).
   - Human summary: 1–3 lines explaining outcome and recommended follow-up.

3) Approval gate integration
   - When a change triggers an approval gate, the gate must record evaluation input hashed into the capsule so external
     auditors can re-evaluate the decision without seeing raw inputs.
   - Gates should be able to attach conditional advice (e.g., require canary or manual approval) that becomes part of the capsule.

4) Retention & minimization policies
   - Tiered retention: default short-term retention (90 days) for full capsules + debug bundles; long-term retention (7+
     years) for compact proofsets only (hashes, merkle roots, signed receipts).
   - Auto-minify: after short-term TTL, platform purges debug bundles and stores only capsule header + receipts + compact
     proofset (no blinded diffs by default unless retention level is high and allowed by customer).
   - Customer control: customers can opt into longer debug retention for support SLAs or opt for more aggressive minimization
     for compliance reasons.

5) Audit & export
   - Export interface to produce a sealed audit package (capsules + chain of receipts + de-obfuscation keys if customer
     permitted) suitable for internal GRC or third-party auditors.
   - Audit package must support both redacted and fully deobfuscated modes controlled by key escrow (customer or joint).

Non-functional requirements
- Performance: swivel operations should not add more than a 200ms median overhead to existing rotation APIs; smoke tests
  should be parallelized and time-boxed.
- Security: capsules signed with platform HSM-backed signing key. De-obfuscation keys are never stored without customer
  consent and must require multi-party unlock for sensitive access.
- Scalability: evidence capsule generation should scale horizontally and not block the swivel critical path (generate cassette
  asynchronously but atomically linked to swivel result).
- Privacy: default mode must never leak raw secrets, private IP addresses, or customer-specific PII in long-term storage.

UX flows (operator + console)
- Console: 'Rotate secret' modal with clear indication which customers will be affected, consent requirement toggle, canary
  options, and visible rollback window. After swivel completes, show capsule summary with link to "View capsule" which shows
  blinded diff and human summary.
- CLI: flags for --mode, --consent-webhook, --debug-ttl. Commands return capsule-id on success.

APIs (sketch)
- POST /v1/private/secrets/{id}/swivel  -> returns { capsule_id, status }
- GET /v1/private/capsules/{capsule_id} -> returns capsule (redacted according to caller permissions)
- POST /v1/private/capsules/{capsule_id}/request-deobfuscation -> initiates multi-party unlock flow

Operational runbook (operator scenarios)
- Success path: swivel -> smoke test pass -> finalize -> capsule created -> notify customer (if configured).
- Smoke fail: auto rollback -> capsule created with failure receipt and attached smoke logs (short TTL).
- Manual rollback: operator triggers rollback within window -> capsule includes operator reason and rollback receipt.
- Escalation: if capsule indicates repeated failures, platform creates an "investigation" event and suggests contacting SRE.

Rollout plan (phases)
- Phase 0: internal beta for Redwood-managed sandboxes (no customer consent). Test capsule format and retention logic.
- Phase 1: invite small set of enterprise customers for opt-in pilot (support-extended debug bundles).
- Phase 2: default opt-out availability for all private deployments with UI/CLI.
- Phase 3: hardened UIs, multi-party deobfuscation, compliance export features.

Open questions and risks
- Legal: do customers require a guaranteed minimum retention window for forensic obligations? Need legal input per region.
- Key escrow model: who holds de-obfuscation keys by default — customer, Redwood, or joint escrow? Tradeoffs for support speed vs. security.
- Policy complexity: approval gates may need richer policy expression to describe network-affecting changes; policy language work
  may be non-trivial.
- UX friction: how to make consent requests unobtrusive in high-frequency maintenance windows?

Next steps / deliverables
- Align with legal/security on escrow model (owner: Priya Shah) — due 2026-03-24.
- Prototype capsule schema and signer integration (owner: Miguel) — spike by 2026-04-07.
- Implement swivel CLI + console flow (MVP) and gated pilot for 3 customers (owner: Ethan) — target 2026-06-15.

Appendix: example capsule (redacted human-ready view)
- Capsule ID: CAPS-20260310-0007
- Time: 2026-03-10T18:11:04Z
- Actor: aisha.patel@redwood (operator)
- Customer ack: alpha-retail-admin@cust (consented)
- Action: rotate-edge-psk (canary)
- Targets: edge-conn-1234 (blinded as conn-AB12)
- Outcome: success
- Smoke tests: tls-handshake(pass), ping(canary-az1)(pass)
- Receipts: platform-signature=SIG-xxx, merkle-root=MR-abc123
- Human summary: "Canary rotation of edge PSK for conn-AB12 succeeded. No downstream route changes. Rollout to the rest of the fleet scheduled in 30m."

(End)
